A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by Chidambaram and Ge. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained experiments across renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original trained-model test errors and weight-norm analyses on modified binary CIFAR tasks and background-shifted MNIST, averaged over five training runs.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds standard CIFAR experiments with ResNets, synthetic classification experiments, and activation/output-variance analyses in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The ERM/weight-decay, label-smoothing, and Mixup objectives and augmentation procedures in Section 2 remain substantively unchanged. ResNets and synthetic experiments extend the evaluation of these existing methods; no new algorithm or augmentation rule is introduced.

E1.justification: v3 adds full multiclass CIFAR-10/100 classification without injected spurious correlations, beyond v2's modified two-class subsets. Appendices C.1-C.2 add two-dimensional and ten-dimensional synthetic datasets. The original binary CIFAR and background-permuted MNIST tasks remain; shaded MNIST becoming colored MNIST is a rename.

E2.justification: ERM with optional weight decay remains the comparator for label smoothing and Mixup. The retained experiments preserve their comparator membership. New ResNet experiments compare the same training families with shared weight decay; no additional competing algorithm is evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 introduces ResNet-18/50/101 protocols, 200-epoch AdamW training, crop/flip augmentation, activation/output-variance metrics, and separate synthetic protocols. For retained binary CIFAR, v2 specifies 100 epochs, Adam, and batch size 500; v3 instead references Section 4.1's settings but subsequently still says Adam. This ambiguously revises the documented protocol without establishing that the retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine activation/output-variance trajectories, target-only versus total output variance, synthetic decision boundaries, and high-variance feature weights. v3 also reports sensitivity checks involving feature scales, added noise, and adding weight decay to label smoothing/Mixup. The original weight-norm-ratio and MNIST background-shift analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over five training runs with one-standard-deviation uncertainty. v3 extends that convention to additional tables and plots, without changing the stated replication count or introducing seed specifications, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive numerical and qualitative results. Table 1 reports ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 test errors of 8.40, 7.96, and 5.90 for ERM+WD, ERM+WD+LS, and ERM+WD+Mixup. Appendix C adds synthetic and deeper-ResNet findings, including higher final activation variances for augmented ResNet-101 models in Table 5. v2 Figures 1-3 remain unchanged as v3 Figures 2-4; the additions are not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Propositions 3.9-3.10 and Appendix A.3 replace conditional variances with variances of conditional expectations: for example, Var(g(X) | Y=y) becomes Var(E[g(X) | Y=y]). For fixed conditioning values, the new terms vanish, materially weakening the written bounds. v3 also expands Corollary 3.4's proof, adds a class-balance qualification, and introduces synthetic-data Definition C.2.

C1.justification: v2 emphasizes the negative consequence of learning low-variance spurious correlations. v3 adds a central positive claim that lower-variance hidden representations correlate with better standard-benchmark performance, framing the phenomenon as both beneficial and harmful. This substantially broadens the abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion while retaining the original theoretical separation and failure claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds a useful-latent-feature hypothesis, an explicit correlation-versus-causation caveat, an Adam/nonconvergence explanation for ERM failures, compact-support applicability qualifications, and discussion of unexplained activation-variance oscillations. Appendix C.4 interprets output variance beyond target-class variability. The standalone limitations paragraph disappears, but the lack of nonlinear optimization-dynamics analysis remains acknowledged in the theoretical discussion and Appendix B.

D1.justification: v3 supplies substantial new implementation information for synthetic data generation and ResNet training, including sample sizes, augmentations, optimizers, and depth-specific batch sizes. Reported hardware changes from P100 to A5000. A new reproducibility statement says supplementary code includes figure-generation instructions, although availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Some explicit binary-subset counts and training details from v2 are omitted or replaced by cross-references.

R1.justification: v3 adds substantive positioning around neural collapse, citing Papyan, Kornblith, Zhou, and Guo, and discusses selective-classification findings from Zhu and Xia. Appendix B substantially expands comparisons with Chidambaram et al. (2023) and Zou et al. (2023), distinguishing population linear minimizers from patch-based neural-network training dynamics.

P1.justification: The contribution list is rewritten around a central message, the abstract and conclusion are reframed, and the experimental narrative now presents standard-benchmark benefits before spurious-correlation failures. Existing experimental descriptions are condensed and reorganized, theoretical motivation is expanded, and separate ethics and reproducibility statements are introduced.

P2.justification: v3 adds multi-panel error/variance trajectories, synthetic decision-boundary and weight-norm plots, and nine numerical tables. The original three figures are retained, resized, and renumbered within a larger set of eight figures. Conversion to the ICLR template also changes typography, title/author formatting, headers, text width, and figure placement.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially broadens v2's restricted empirical support through standard CIFAR/ResNet experiments, synthetic checks, and useful diagnostic and implementation detail. However, the revised Propositions 3.9-3.10 make their variance penalties vanish as written, and unchanged experimental plots accompany ambiguous revised training descriptions. Table 5 also qualifies the broader low-activation-variance claim. These material theoretical and reproducibility problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the empirical gains.
